threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look puzzled when you see the 'Not in Service' sign on a Tube train. You think it's broken, but really, it’s just the way of life here.
Caught a whiff of jerk chicken on the 35 last night; turns out the guy next to me had a full takeout tucked away. Smell was better company than him.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a bus the other day, and the driver hopped out to grab a snack from the Kiosk, all while the passengers just waited. Classic Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar that serves drinks in old soup cans. It’s a quirky twist that blends nostalgia with nightlife.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local if they know to avoid the 14-Mission during rush hour. Tourists just think it’s an Uber problem.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo hop on the 31 at Civic Center after a wedding. He smiled and said, 'Nothing says love like a crowded bus ride home.' Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all bohemian charm, but many locals avoid it during festival time—too many drumming tourists drown out our evenings.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for a 'café con leche' but pronounce it like it's a spell from Harry Potter. It's always 'café con letche' around here.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers: they still queue for the 106 bus instead of walking to the next stop like everyone else.
Last night on the 196, I watched a guy try to pay with an old £1 coin. The driver just shook his head but the next passenger handed him a donut instead.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home was when I heard a street musician playing accordion at 3 a.m. while people outside debated the best döner in town.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery. It’s a strange mix of grilled meat and abstract expressionism, but it works.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their reaction to the BART delays; non-locals panic, while we just pull out snacks and settle in for the wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 Fulton halted for a dog on the tracks yesterday. Drivers had to wait while a guy coaxed it with treats—only in SF!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for Instagram. But locals know they’re the heartbeats where impromptu concerts and chess games pop up.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily: they still stare in awe at the TNC trailers outside the metro, trying to decipher if it's a food truck or a film set.
